ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows four labeled logic-symbol circuits. Circuit A has two inputs A and B entering a rectangular block marked with '&', with output Y on the right and no output bubble. Circuit B has inputs A and B entering a rectangular block marked '=1', with output Y on the right and no output bubble. Circuit C has inputs A and B entering a rectangular block marked with '&', and its output to Y includes a small circle/bubble at the output. Circuit D has inputs A and B entering a rectangular block marked '≥1', with output Y on the right and no output bubble. Reasoning: A NAND gate is an AND gate followed by inversion at the output. In this symbol style, AND is indicated by '&', and inversion is indicated by a small output bubble. Among the labeled circuits, only circuit C has both the '&' symbol and the output bubble. Therefore the NAND gate is circuit C.
